text: This slice writes its own tables: interaction and contact_point_ext are P1's in rwb_source_data (the ledger by the R-PREC default ruling and DP-18, the extension table by the Ownership Map), so the cutover load inserts the migrated rows on the service's own login on its own Flyway sequence, and recovery_case is read through the P3 rwb-case contract and never written.
why: The Ownership Map gives both tables to P1 and recovery_case to P3, and DP-01 forbids a write to another service's schema, so the load has to be this service's or it has no lawful owner.
read: Ownership Map interaction (P1, ASM-A6-tables-1), contact_point_ext (P1) and recovery_case (P3); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-01, DP-15 and DP-18; Architecture v5 slides 29 and 41
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check
impact: Medium: the load is one service's own work and needs no handover, so the story builds without a C or I dependency.

text: The person key and the contact key of a migrated interaction are carried as the ACE business keys the legacy row holds and are not translated into party_id or contact_point_id: the migration resolves no cross-reference, invents no identifier and writes no row of another table for them.
why: The legacy AC1 keeps person_key and contact_key, the only column list of the ledger names party_id and contact_point_id as cross-references, and a migration that minted a uuid for either would create a reference to a row that never existed.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-005 AC1 and Data table; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 (interaction DF-INT-003, DF-INT-022); TSD P1 v3 T3.3 views 3 and 4 and T3.9 business-key links
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check
impact: Medium: the two business keys stay resolvable by REC-05 and no orphan reference is created at cutover.

text: The DM-005 cutover load writes the legacy consent and contact-quality rows into contact_point_ext, keyed by contact_key, with consent carried as consent_given plus consent_at (a WITHDRAWN status as false with its date and an UNKNOWN status as no row), while RWB-P1-DM002-APP reads the table for DP02 and writes none of it.
why: The legacy DM-005 data row is the only place the consent rows are named for cutover and no other slice carries them, while the FSD files the table under DP02 and gives DP05 only interaction.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-005 Data table (DF-EXT-013 to DF-EXT-026); FSD P1 v3 A2.2 DP02 and DP05 rows; TSD P1 v3 T3.5 and its consent mapping note; Ownership Map contact_point_ext (P1)
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check
impact: Low: the rows are read by the DP02 read path whether or not a later slice reloads them.

text: The ten clean days are counted from the reconciliation_result rows JOB-04 writes for the migrated records: a PASS row with no unexplained variance and no new REC-05 orphan extends the count by one day, a BREAK row or a new orphan resets it to zero, and no counter table is created for the count.
why: The legacy AC3 says 'ten clean days' without saying where the count lives, and JOB-04 already writes one row per check and product group with a PASS or BREAK result and lists the REC-05 orphans.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-005 AC3; FSD P1 v3 A2.11.2 and A2.11.3.1 (BR-P1-011-3); TSD P1 v3 T3.6 reconciliation_result DF-OPS-118 to DF-OPS-129; DL25
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check
impact: Low: the evidence is read from rows the reconciliation already writes and no new table is needed.

text: The cutover record of the release pipeline holds what the cutover did and what it proved: the business date, the counts read, skipped and written, the legacy record keys, the ten day rows with the reconciliation extract they came from, and the data steward's sign-off; nothing is written to a schema for any of it, and the extract's format, file name and dump layout are fixed at the cutover rehearsal and recorded in this story's Flyway description.
why: Legacy AC3 requires a sign-off after ten clean days and no source gives a table, a file or an operation for either the count or the sign-off, while Architecture v5 slide 32 makes one-off bulk work a release-pipeline step that never touches a rwb_* schema.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-005 AC3; Architecture v5 slide 32 ('One-off bulk work', 'Airflow never reads or writes rwb_* schemas'); TSD P1 v3 T3.2
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check
impact: Medium: the evidence lives with the release and not in a table, so a reader finds it in the cutover record and the Flyway history together.

text: This story owns legacy AC3 only: legacy AC1 and AC2 move to RWB-ITG-DM005-ITG, whose harness proves the five kept facts and the no-copy rule and the REC-05 reconciliation of the business keys against this service's contract, and the legacy test cases TC-DM-005-01 and TC-DM-005-02 sit there as -ITG copies.
why: The split plan assigns AC1 and AC2 to the wave 4 integration story of the same legacy key and AC3 to this slice, and the case of each migrated interaction is then answered by the P3 contract mock rather than claimed as a build dependency.
read: Split plan for RWB-DM-005 (slices and AC ownership); RWB-ITG-DM005-ITG section 7 and section 16
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check
impact: None: the two slices meet at the published contract and neither claims the other's criteria.

text: The cutover step sits behind the platform feature switch rwb.source-data.dm005-cutover-extract, default off: off, the step refuses to start and writes no row, and the Flyway version still applies because it creates nothing.
why: The platform flag library owns feature flags (R-PREC default ruling) and a one-off cutover must be startable and not startable by configuration, while a migration that creates nothing is safe to apply in every environment.
read: Template and Rules v1 §R3 default ruling (feature flags to the platform library) and §R5.5 DP-15; TSD P1 v3 T3.2
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check
impact: Low: the switch gates the load only and never the schema.

text: P1 extracts the legacy listing, case asset link and sale instruction rows and hands them to S5 in one package per cutover business date; S5 loads them into rwb_asset on S5's own Flyway sequence, and P1 writes no row of rwb_asset.
why: The Ownership Map puts listing and asset_sale with S5 and DP-01 forbids a write into another service's schema, while the legacy story moves them in one cutover with no owner named.
read: Ownership Map listing and asset_sale (owner S5, Architecture v5 slide 41 and TSD S5 v2 T3.1); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-01 and DP-15; legacy RWB-DM-006 AC1
confirm: Solution architect with the S5 rwb-asset tech lead at the wave 4 entry check
impact: Medium: the load owner is S5 and the extract owner is P1, so the package layout and the cutover rehearsal are the only moving parts.

text: P1 loads valuation_ext itself on the next free version of its own Flyway sequence, 1:1 on the primary key valuation_key, with the six appraisal decision fields and the seven standard record columns, and no ACE appraisal column is copied into it.
why: valuation_ext is the one table of the legacy key that the Ownership Map keeps with P1, and the table already exists from the V0001 baseline, so the cutover carries rows and no schema change.
read: Ownership Map valuation_ext (owner P1, ruling plus ASM-A6-tables-15); TSD P1 v3 T3.2, T3.5 and T3.0; FSD P1 v3 AC-P1-001-01
confirm: Data steward and the P1 recovery tech lead at the wave 4 entry check
impact: None on other stories; a wrong reading would move the acceptance out of P1 into S1 and add a C dependency that this key does not hold.

text: The legacy case asset link is carried on the handover row as the case key beside the asset_key and lands in no table of its own, because the Ownership Map and LDM v8 give it none; the link is proved through v_ace_collateral and the account keys the case links.
why: AC1 names the case asset link among the records read at cutover but asserts only the asset_key of a listing and of a sale, and no source names a target table for the link itself.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-006 AC1 and story text; TSD P1 v3 T3.3 view 7 v_ace_collateral key asset_key and account_key; LDM v8 case_account DF-CAS-024 to DF-CAS-029 and table inventory
confirm: Solution architect with the data steward at the wave 4 entry check
impact: Low: the link is carried and proved, not stored, and no new table is created by this story.

text: Ten clean days are counted from the reconciliation_result rows of JOB-04 on the migrated records: a PASS day with no unexplained variance, no new REC-05 orphan and a LOADED DP06 stamp extends the count, and a BREAK row, a new orphan or a STALE DP06 day resets it to zero.
why: AC3 requires ten consecutive clean days without defining one, and DP06 is a WEEKLY product whose stamp can be a week old on a day JOB-04 passes, so the two signals have to be joined explicitly.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-006 AC3; FSD P1 v3 A2.2 (DP06 WEEKLY, MON 08:00), A2.11.2, A2.14.2 and BR-P1-014-3; TSD P1 v3 T3.6; DL25
confirm: Data steward at the wave 4 entry check
impact: Medium: a STALE DP06 day delays the sign-off rather than failing the cutover, and the count is read from rows that already exist.

text: The ten day rows, the DP06 stamps, the reconciliation extract and the data steward's sign-off are held in the cutover record of the release pipeline; no counter table and no sign-off table is created and nothing is written to a schema for them.
why: AC3 requires the sign-off but names no store, and the sibling cutover slices of this service hold their evidence the same way, so the pipeline record is the one place already carrying the run.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-006 AC3; Template and Rules v1 §R9 (a missing value is a gap and an assumption); Architecture v5 slide 32 (the release pipeline runs one-off bulk work against the APIs)
confirm: Data steward and release manager at the wave 4 entry check
impact: Low: the evidence is read from the reconciliation rows and from the catalog stamps, and no new table is granted.

text: The asset_key proof runs against v_ace_asset and v_ace_collateral from Day 1 and the valuation_key proof against v_ace_valuation from the week RWB-ACE-001 lands and against its contract fake before; the appraisal acceptance rows are loaded either way, and the cutover stays behind its feature switch while the Section B views are absent.
why: v_ace_valuation and v_ace_batch_status are Section B views that ship with RWB-ACE-001, and no source says how the cutover behaves in the gap between this story's build and that deployment.
read: TSD P1 v3 T3.2 and T3.3 views 17 and 18; FSD P1 v3 OQ-P1-01, OQ-P1-02 and A2.14.2; Decision Log DL43
confirm: Solution architect with the ACE team lead at the wave 4 entry check
impact: Medium: until RWB-ACE-001 lands no day can count as clean, so the sign-off waits on the ACE team and not on this story.

text: The feature switch rwb.source-data.dm006-cutover-extract, taken from the platform flag library, defaults to off: off, the cutover step refuses to start and no package leaves, while the migration still applies because it creates no object.
why: The platform flag library owns the flag defaults and no source fixes the value of a per-story switch, so the safe default is stated rather than assumed silently.
read: Template and Rules v1 §R3 (feature flags owned by the platform library); Architecture v5 slide 32 (bulk cutover runs from the release pipeline)
confirm: DevOps lead at the wave 4 entry check
impact: Low: a wrong default keeps the cutover closed and is changed by a flag row, not by a code change.

text: Legacy AC2 Reconcile the business keys, its REC-05 orphan list across the services and legacy TC-DM-006-02 sit with RWB-ITG-DM006-ITG as TC-DM-006-02-ITG; this slice owns AC1, AC3 and TC-DM-006-01, TC-DM-006-03 and TC-DM-006-04 only.
why: The split plan gives AC1 and AC3 of the legacy key to RWB-P1-DM006-APP, and the ITG story is the one that exercises the reconciliation across the owning services.
read: Split plan metadata of RWB-P1-DM006-APP (acs AC1, AC3) and of RWB-ITG-DM006-ITG; legacy RWB-DM-006 AC2 and test cases
confirm: Integration lead at the wave 4 entry check
impact: None: the AC2 copy and the ITG test copies live on the ITG story and are not repeated here.

text: Each owner loads its own rows: S4 rwb-litigation loads legal_action into rwb_litigation, P6 rwb-comms loads notice into rwb_comms and S9 rwb-partner loads partner_instruction into rwb_partner, each on its own Flyway sequence, and P1 extracts and hands over and holds no INSERT against another service's schema.

read: Ownership Map legal_action (S4), notice (P6) and partner_instruction (S9); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 41 and 45; Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-01 and DP-15
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check

text: The extract leaves as one handover package per owner per cutover business date, written to the cutover record of the release pipeline and not to a table; the package layout, its file format and the point where the pipeline writes it are agreed at the cutover rehearsal and are not fixed here.
why: No source gives a package shape, and the legacy key names only a cutover step run by the recovery service identity with its breaks on the reconciliation extract.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-007 Endpoints and AC1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 32 One-off bulk work and Airflow never reads or writes rwb_* schemas
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check
impact: A package format change is a rehearsal decision and changes no criterion.

text: The partner instruction is handed over in two slices: this story carries the instruction raised for a legal action with the instruction id, the case, the firm, the instruction type, the instructed_at and the due_at, and RWB-P1-DM008-APP carries the panel performance facts of the same instruction; S9 loads both packages, idempotent on the instruction id.
why: partner_instruction appears in the data table of both RWB-DM-007 and RWB-DM-008 and the table has one owner, so the two migrations must not duplicate the row.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-007 Data table partner_instruction DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016 and AC1; legacy RWB-DM-008 story; Ownership Map partner_instruction (S9)
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check
impact: A wrong split would leave a firm with a due date and no performance record, or a performance record with no clock.

text: Ten clean days are counted from the reconciliation_result rows JOB-04 writes for the migrated records, one set per business date: a PASS row with no unexplained variance and no new REC-05 orphan extends the count, and a BREAK row or a new orphan resets it to zero and names the day.
why: AC3 states the outcome only and no source gives the count its rows, its reset rule or its threshold.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-007 AC3; FSD P1 v3 A2.11.2 and A2.11.3.1; TSD P1 v3 T3.6 reconciliation_result with result PASS or BREAK; DL25
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check
impact: A reset-on-break rule is stricter than a checklist and is the evidence the data steward signs; a different rule would reopen a cutover after a single break.

text: The cutover record of the release pipeline holds the extract definition, the three owner packages, the ten day rows and the data steward's sign-off, and the release pipeline runs the cutover as one-off bulk work through the service's own admin operations and never reads or writes a rwb_* schema.
why: AC3 requires a sign-off and a read-only window without naming a store, and Architecture v5 slide 32 puts cutover loads on service APIs and not on schemas.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 32 One-off bulk work and its notes; legacy RWB-DM-007 AC3; TSD P1 v3 Appendix T-A API-P1-002 and API-P1-003
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check
impact: A record kept elsewhere would need a store and a retention rule and would add a table this story does not own.

text: The feature switch is rwb.source-data.dm007-cutover-extract from the platform flag library and it defaults off: off, the cutover step refuses to start and no package is handed over, and the migration still applies because it creates nothing.
why: The legacy story has no switch, the platform naming rule gives the service prefix, and a bulk cutover must not run before the cutover rehearsal and the owners' loads.
read: Template and Rules §R3 default ruling Feature flags to the platform library; Template and Rules §R4 naming; split plan patterns DP05, DP15 and DP19
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check
impact: A wrong default would let a cutover start before the owners' loads are ready; the schema change is unaffected.

text: Legacy AC1 and AC2 of RWB-DM-007 sit with RWB-ITG-DM007-ITG, so this P1 slice claims AC3 only, keeps TC-DM-007-03 and TC-DM-007-04, and leaves TC-DM-007-01 and TC-DM-007-02 with the integration story as the -ITG copies.

read: split plan of RWB-DM-007 with acs AC3 for RWB-P1-DM007-APP and AC1, AC2 for RWB-ITG-DM007-ITG; RWB-ITG-DM007-ITG sections 7 and 16
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check

text: The story carries Status Draft (realignment v1) because no approval of the realigned story is recorded, and the release 31 December 2026 is copied unchanged and marked tentative.

read: legacy RWB-DM-007 Epic E2, release 31 December 2026; D-RCV-60 overlay; Template and Rules §R1 U7
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check

text: No lawsuit and no hearing record is copied: this story resolves the legacy lawsuit_no with one read of v_ace_lawsuit as a proof and stores nothing of the view, v_ace_hearing and v_ace_pod are read by the DP07 record read and the REC-05 step and not by the cutover, and the key-resolution proof stays with RWB-P1-E1011-APP and RWB-ITG-DM007-ITG.

read: legacy RWB-DM-007 AC1; TSD P1 v3 T3.2 and T3.3 views 22 to 24; FSD P1 v3 A2.2.2 DP07; ADR-010; DL43
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check

text: S9 rwb-partner loads the migrated partner, partner user and partner instruction rows into rwb_partner on S9's own Flyway sequence, and P1 writes no row of that schema.
why: DP-01 forbids a service from reading or writing another service's tables, the Ownership Map gives the three tables to S9 in rwb_partner, and Architecture v5 slides 29 and 45 enforce ownership by grants and keep one reader of the ACE views; the integration story's sentence that reads the load as P1's own sequence is read as the handover it describes.
read: Ownership Map tables partner, partner_user and partner_instruction (S9, rwb_partner; ASM-A6-tables-6); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 29, 41 and 45; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01 and DP-15; RWB-ITG-DM008-ITG sections 1 and 19
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check

text: This story hands over the panel, the partner users and the performance facts of the partner instructions, and RWB-DM-007 hands over the instructions raised for legal actions; both packages carry the instruction id and S9 loads them idempotently on it.
why: partner_instruction appears in both legacy keys with the same field range DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016 and no source rules the split, so the duplication has to be ruled or the service would receive two partial instruction rows for one instruction id.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-007 AC1 and data row; legacy RWB-DM-008 AC1 and data row; FSD P1 v3 A2.2.2 DP08 row; TSD P1 v3 T3.6 and T3.7
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check

text: Ten clean days are counted from the reconciliation_result rows that JOB-04 writes for the business dates after the load: a PASS row with no unexplained variance and no new REC-05 orphan on a key this cutover handed over extends the count, and a BREAK row or a new orphan resets it to zero.
why: Legacy AC3 names ten clean days without saying which record proves a clean day, and reconciliation_result is the only table the platform writes per business date with a PASS or BREAK result and the REC-05 orphan leg.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-008 AC3; FSD P1 v3 A2.11.2 and A2.11.4; TSD P1 v3 T3.6 (reconciliation_result DF-OPS-118 to DF-OPS-129 and the REC-05 row); Architecture v5 slide 44 JOB-04
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check
impact: The clean-day gate is a reconciliation gate and not a partner-record gate; a day whose reconciliation did not run cannot be counted as clean, and the sign-off stays closed.

text: DP08 Partner performance is a Workbench product, refreshed ON_CHANGE with no ACE system of record and no v_ace_* view behind it, so the migrated records carry no ACE freshness stamp and their recency is proved by the reconciliation rows rather than by a data_product_load row; this key reads no view at all and DP-05 applies in its boundary form only.
why: The freshness model writes data_product_load from v_ace_batch_status for source-fed products and names the Workbench products as current on change, so a stamp for DP08 would be a provenance the product does not have; waiting for an ACE batch for DP08 would never end.
read: FSD P1 v3 A2.2.2 (DP08 row) and A2.14.2; TSD P1 v3 T3.6 (data_product_load), T3.7; Architecture v5 slide 45
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check
impact: No freshness answer is published for DP08 from this cutover; a consumer that expects a DP08 stamp will not find one, and the ITG harness must read the reconciliation result instead.

text: The cutover step is one-off bulk work started from the release pipeline for one business date, and its cutover record holds the handover package, the ten day rows, the reconciliation extract they came from and the data steward's sign-off.
why: Architecture v5 slide 32 gives cutover loads to the bank pipeline against the P1 and P8 APIs and never their schemas, and legacy AC3 names a sign-off without naming where it is kept; the record is the only place the evidence can live without inventing a table.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 32 and 44; legacy RWB-DM-008 AC1, AC3 and Endpoints rows; FSD P1 v3 A2.13
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check
impact: The evidence has no schema home: an audit that needs the ten day rows in a table rather than in the pipeline record would need a further story.

text: The feature switch rwb.source-data.dm008-cutover-extract defaults to off in every environment until the cutover rehearsal, and the migration applies whether the switch is on or off because it creates nothing.

read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-15 and R7.2 s13; RWB-P1-DM004-APP section 13 (the sibling cutover switch)
confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check

text: Legacy AC1 and AC2 sit with RWB-ITG-DM008-ITG and this P1 slice owns legacy AC3 only, so TC-DM-008-01 and TC-DM-008-02 are the ITG copies and the two cases here are TC-DM-008-03 and TC-DM-008-04.
why: The split plan allots AC1 and AC2 to the integration story and AC3 to the P1 slice, and the integration harness is the place where the business keys of the three partner tables are proved across the services.

confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check
impact: This story's acceptance is the cutover evidence and the boundary only; the extract facts and the key reconciliation are accepted on the integration story, so a defect there is fixed there.

text: The story carries Status Draft (realignment v1) because no approval of the realigned story is recorded, and the run takes no approval step.

P1 writes no other service's schema, holds no INSERT against rwb_debtsale and joins nothing across the boundary.

confirm: Solution architect at the wave 4 entry check

Because DP09 is ON_CHANGE with no ACE source system and no freshness stamp, these rows are the only recency proof the cutover can hold, and no counter table is created.

confirm: Data steward

text: The data steward's sign-off and the ten day rows behind it are held in the cutover record of the release pipeline, with the reconciliation extract they came from and the read-only window of the legacy tables; no sign-off table is created in rwb_source_data.
why: The legacy AC3 requires a sign-off and a read-only period, and no source gives a table or a store for either.

confirm: Release manager and data steward

text: The feature switch rwb.source-data.dm009-cutover-extract defaults to off: while it is off the cutover step refuses to start and no package is handed over, and the Flyway version still applies because it creates no table, column or index.
why: No source gives a default for the switch, and a cutover extract that runs before the views and the reconciliation are live would hand over rows nothing can reconcile.

confirm: DevOps lead
